questions.q: What does a transaction isolation level fundamentally control?
options: How much protection a transaction gets from seeing other transactions' in-progress changes, trading consistency against concurrency
How fast a query runs, independent of any other session
Whether a transaction can be rolled back at all
Which columns a query is allowed to SELECT
questions.explain: Isolation level is a dial: stricter settings prevent more anomalies but cause more blocking; looser settings allow more concurrency but more anomalies.

questions.q: Which statement sets the isolation level for the current session?
options: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL <level>;
ALTER SESSION SET ISOLATION <level>;
BEGIN TRANSACTION ISOLATION <level>;
SET LOCK_TIMEOUT <level>;
questions.explain: SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL is the T-SQL statement, e.g. SET TRANSACTION ISOLATION LEVEL READ COMMITTED;

questions.q: What are the four ANSI standard isolation levels, from loosest to strictest?
options: READ UNCOMMITTED, READ COMMITTED, REPEATABLE READ, SERIALIZABLE
SNAPSHOT, RCSI, READ COMMITTED, SERIALIZABLE
READ COMMITTED, READ UNCOMMITTED, SERIALIZABLE, REPEATABLE READ
LOCKED, UNLOCKED, VERSIONED, STRICT
questions.explain: These four are defined by the SQL standard and all implemented by SQL Server, each preventing strictly more anomalies than the last.

questions.q: What are SQL Server's own additions beyond the four ANSI levels?
options: SNAPSHOT (a session-level isolation level) and RCSI (a database-level setting), both based on row versioning
FAST and SLOW, two performance presets
LOCKED and UNLOCKED, two locking modes
There are no additions — SQL Server only implements the four ANSI levels
questions.explain: SNAPSHOT and Read Committed Snapshot Isolation (RCSI) are SQL Server-specific, row-versioning-based mechanisms not required by the ANSI standard.

questions.q: What are the three classic read anomalies previewed in this lesson?
options: Dirty read, nonrepeatable read, and phantom read
Deadlock, blocking, and lock escalation
Shared lock, exclusive lock, and update lock
Rollback, commit, and savepoint
questions.explain: These three anomalies are what the next three lessons cover in depth, and what every isolation level is defined in terms of preventing or allowing.
